text:
The Fed didn't cut rates to zero in 2024. It began easing in September 2024 with a 50 bp cut, followed by 25 bp cuts in November and December, which brought the federal funds target range to 4.25%-4.50%. The reasons were inflation cooling toward 2% and a softening labor market.

The last times the Fed took rates to near zero (0-0.25%) were December 2008 (financial crisis) and March 2020 (COVID).

If you saw a claim about zero rates in 2024, it was wrong, or it may have been confusing the Fed with another central bank, such as the Bank of Japan, which was near zero until its March 2024 hike.
